title: Greece's transport ministry presents an AI system to transcribe stationmaster-driver GSM-R dialogues in real time and check them against protocols
summary: CNN.gr (18 May 2026): Deputy Minister Konstantinos Kyranakis presented a system that converts GSM-R audio to text and uses AI to check compliance with traffic protocols, described as a safety valve...
account: CNN.gr reported on Monday 18 May 2026 that Deputy Minister of Transport Konstantinos Kyranakis had presented, the previous Saturday, an artificial-intelligence system that converts in real time the dialogues between stationmasters and train drivers carried over the GSM-R radio system into text and uses AI to determine whether the text is within the strict traffic-regulation protocols, so that the control center knows when it must intervene; he described it as a serious safety valve that changes the lax mentality that used to exist on the railway, a reference to the dialogue patterns exposed after the Tempi disaster. The article gives no developer, start date or results and the system is presented as planned; the OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry (2026-05-18-b527) notes that no incidents had yet occurred. The date given is the publication date.
purpose: The system is intended to monitor operational radio communications and flag departures from protocol for the control center.
system: Speech-to-text and AI protocol-compliance monitoring of GSM-R stationmaster-driver communications (supplier not named)
deployer: Hellenic Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (planned)
taxonomy_note: Announcement only; compliance checking of rail communications is read as a safety detection mechanism.

ai_role.statement: Described function only; accuracy of transcription and protocol classification, and how the control center acts on alerts, are not reported.
